memories.content: The instructions for one medication the user takes say to take it after the evening meal.
On a day with a morning appointment, the user miscalculated the fasting period and checked again at the reception desk.
For an afternoon visit, the user felt less rushed while preparing to travel than for a morning visit.
On a day there was no waiting chair, the user stood for 20 minutes and their back became uncomfortable.
On a day medication instructions were explained all at once and at length, the user failed to write down an important time.
On a day medication times were confirmed one line at a time, the user copied them directly into their schedule after returning home.
On a visit when their younger brother drove them, the user did not have to find a separate route home.
The user's younger brother prefers to receive a request for weekday-afternoon transportation two days beforehand rather than on the day itself.
The local agent cannot determine the current prescription or whether use continues from medication notes alone.
The waiting area at that clinic has too few chairs, so there may be periods when people must wait standing.
The user keeps the shared laundry-room access card in an entrance drawer.
The user went downstairs 25 minutes after the laundry finished and received a note from another household.
For the next load, the user set a reminder five minutes before the end and removed the laundry immediately.
The user washed light-colored clothes with new jeans, and color transferred onto white socks.
The user later washed the new jeans separately, and the color of the other clothes did not change.
On a day the user did not check the dryer filter, the clothes needed another drying cycle.
On the next use, after emptying the filter, the user finished drying in one cycle.
The building manager judges that not leaving finished laundry for a long time is fair to other households.
When creating a shared laundry-room reminder, base it on the end time of the machine the user started.
Even if the local agent knows where the card is kept, it cannot know which machines in the shared laundry room are currently available.

analysis.overview: The frames contain independent practical knowledge in separate domains: the reference covers medication handling, clinic visits, waiting conditions, and transportation, while the compared frame covers shared-laundry access, timing, sorting, drying, etiquette, reminders, and availability limits. No cross-frame claim governs the same operational decision.
